props.characteristic: what the elementary learned unit computes
props.positive_test: two models differ here only if their units are of a different kind
props.negative_test: the difference is in how units are wired, which is connectivity

props.characteristic: a weighted sum passed through a nonlinearity
props.positive_test: the unit emits a continuous activation
props.negative_test: the unit emits discrete events in time
props.notes: DEFAULT.

props.characteristic: a membrane potential emitting discrete events in time
props.positive_test: the unit integrates input over time and fires
props.negative_test: the unit emits a continuous value
props.notes: ORTHOGONAL to wiring -- a spiking CNN exists. Both derivation runs made this a lineage ROOT, which would force a spiking CNN to choose. Zero corpus mentions; kept because the ontology covers the field.

props.characteristic: what a parameter is taken to be
props.positive_test: two models differ here only in whether parameters carry uncertainty
props.negative_test: the difference is in the shape or wiring of the model

props.characteristic: each parameter is a single number
props.positive_test: training yields one weight vector
props.negative_test: training yields a distribution, or an explicit set of weight samples
props.notes: DEFAULT.

props.characteristic: parameters carry a distribution
props.positive_test: the model represents uncertainty in its own weights
props.negative_test: uncertainty is represented only in the output layer

props.characteristic: which transformations of the input the model is built to respect
props.positive_test: two models differ here only in the group they are equivariant to
props.negative_test: the invariance is learned from augmentation rather than built in

props.characteristic: no equivariance is imposed by construction
props.positive_test: any invariance is learned
props.negative_test: the architecture guarantees it
props.notes: DEFAULT.

props.characteristic: reordering the inputs reorders the outputs identically
props.positive_test: the model treats its input as a set or graph
props.negative_test: the model depends on input order

props.characteristic: rotating or translating the input transforms the output accordingly
props.positive_test: the architecture guarantees E(n) or SE(3) equivariance
props.negative_test: the symmetry is only encouraged by the loss or by augmentation
props.notes: ORTHOGONAL: the corpus has equivariant GNNs, Transformers, MLPs and mesh networks -- one property across four lineages. Split from invariance 2026-10-06: a corpus quote partitions them outright -- 'Invariant Model: SchNet, DimeNet, SphereNet, GemNet' against 'Vector Frame Basis Equivariant Model: EGNN, PaiNN, GVP' -- and one collapsed value lost the distinction.

props.characteristic: rotating or translating the input leaves the output unchanged
props.positive_test: the output is a scalar or otherwise carries no frame
props.negative_test: the output transforms WITH the input, which is equivariance
props.notes: Added 2026-10-06. Mathematically a special case of equivariance, but the field and the corpus treat them as a partition.

props.characteristic: shifting the input shifts the output
props.positive_test: weight sharing across positions guarantees it
props.negative_test: position-specific weights break it
props.notes: Implied by connectivity=convolution; recorded only where a paper makes it the point.

props.characteristic: whether every parameter participates in every forward pass
props.positive_test: two models differ here only in whether computation is conditional
props.negative_test: the difference is in total parameter count, which belongs to the run

props.characteristic: every parameter is used for every input
props.positive_test: one forward pass touches the whole model
props.negative_test: a gate selects a subset of parameters per input
props.notes: DEFAULT.

props.characteristic: a learned gate selects which parameters run
props.positive_test: active parameter count is lower than total parameter count
props.negative_test: all parameters are always active
props.notes: Makes total vs active parameters diverge, which matters for the Epoch compute estimate.

props.characteristic: whether the model reads and writes an external store
props.positive_test: two models differ here only in the presence of a store outside the weights
props.negative_test: the state is carried in activations, which is recurrence

props.characteristic: all state lives in weights and activations
props.positive_test: the model has no addressable store
props.negative_test: there is a differentiable or retrieved store
props.notes: DEFAULT.

props.characteristic: an addressable store outside the parameters
props.positive_test: the model issues reads and writes against a store
props.negative_test: the store is the input itself
props.examples: Neural Turing Machine; memory networks; retrieval-augmented models
props.notes: Divided 2026-10-06: one value was doing three jobs.

props.characteristic: an addressable store written and read by the model, trained end to end
props.positive_test: gradients flow through the read and write operations
props.negative_test: the store is fixed at inference, or populated by a separate retriever
props.examples: Neural Turing Machine; Differentiable Neural Computer; memory networks

props.characteristic: a fixed store looked up at inference and never trained
props.positive_test: entries are precomputed and the lookup has no learned parameters
props.negative_test: the retriever itself is trained, or the model writes to the store

props.characteristic: a trained retriever selects entries from an external corpus
props.positive_test: the retrieval step has its own learned parameters
props.negative_test: lookup is by fixed similarity, or the store is written by the model

props.characteristic: what the internal representation is taken to be
props.positive_test: two models differ here only in whether the latent is a distribution
props.negative_test: the difference is what the model is trained to output, an objective

props.characteristic: the encoder emits a vector
props.positive_test: one input gives one latent
props.negative_test: the encoder emits distribution parameters and the latent is sampled
props.notes: DEFAULT.

props.characteristic: the encoder emits distribution parameters and the latent is sampled
props.positive_test: the forward pass draws the latent, typically via reparameterization
props.negative_test: the latent is a deterministic function of the input
props.notes: This is the genuine structural residue of the autoencoder question: a VAE encoder emits mu and sigma rather than z, which is a difference in the network and not only in the loss.

props.characteristic: whether the map is constrained to be bijective
props.positive_test: two models differ here only in whether the forward map can be exactly inverted
props.negative_test: the inverse is learned approximately by a second component

props.characteristic: the forward map loses information
props.positive_test: no exact inverse exists
props.negative_test: the architecture guarantees an exact inverse with tractable Jacobian
props.notes: DEFAULT.

props.characteristic: the forward map is bijective with a tractable Jacobian
props.positive_test: the same weights run exactly backwards
props.negative_test: a separate decoder approximates the inverse
props.notes: Owner moved this out of topology on 2026-10-02: invertibility constrains the FUNCTION CLASS, which is what equivariance does, and equivariance is an attribute. A flow is a single stack with invertibility=invertible; its coupling / autoregressive / continuous-time split is LINEAGE substructure.

props.characteristic: whether every position attends to every other
props.positive_test: two models differ here only in which pairs the attention is allowed to score
props.negative_test: the difference is whether attention is present at all, which is connectivity
props.notes: Applies only where connectivity includes attention. Added 2026-10-02: the lineage merge found efficient-attention families homeless on all four axes, and both derivation runs had refused them as lineage nodes.

props.characteristic: every position may attend to every other
props.positive_test: cost grows quadratically with sequence length
props.negative_test: the pattern is restricted, or the softmax is replaced by a kernel feature map
props.notes: DEFAULT.

props.characteristic: only a chosen subset of position pairs is scored
props.positive_test: a fixed or learned pattern restricts which pairs are computed
props.negative_test: all pairs are scored, or attention is linearised by a feature map
props.notes: Changes the compute profile without changing the lineage, which is why it is an attribute.

props.characteristic: the softmax is replaced so cost is linear in length
props.positive_test: attention is computed through a kernel feature map or low-rank factorization
props.negative_test: the full pairwise softmax is computed over a restricted pattern

props.characteristic: the latent is snapped to entries of a learned codebook
props.positive_test: the forward pass replaces the encoder output with its nearest codebook vector
props.negative_test: the latent is a free real vector, or is sampled from a distribution
props.notes: Added 2026-10-06: VQ-VAE resolved to BOTH Deterministic and Stochastic, which is incoherent on a single-valued family. Its latent is neither.

props.characteristic: whether and how information bypasses layers
props.positive_test: two models differ here only in what a shortcut path carries across a block
props.negative_test: the difference is in what the layers themselves compute, which is connectivity
props.notes: Added 2026-10-06 (owner): ResNet's distinctive contribution WAS the skip connection, and the axes could not say so -- ResNet and DenseNet resolved identically. Cross-cutting, which is the test for an attribute: it appears in CNNs, Transformers and U-Nets alike.

props.characteristic: every layer feeds only the next
props.positive_test: signal passes through each block in turn
props.negative_test: a path carries the block input past the block
props.notes: DEFAULT.

props.characteristic: the block input is added to the block output
props.positive_test: the block learns a residual, and identity is the zero-parameter solution
props.negative_test: the bypassed signal is concatenated rather than summed
props.notes: What made ResNet trainable at depth. Shared with Transformer blocks, which is why this is an attribute and not a ResNet-lineage fact.

props.characteristic: the bypassed signal is concatenated to the block output
props.positive_test: channel count grows along the path; earlier features stay separately addressable
props.negative_test: the bypassed signal is summed into the output
props.notes: This is exactly what separates DenseNet from ResNet, and U-Net from a plain encoder-decoder convnet.

props.characteristic: where a model's weights come from
props.positive_test: two models differ here only in whether their weights were trained directly or emitted by another network
props.negative_test: the difference is in what the weights encode, which is lineage, or how they are updated, which is an algorithm

props.characteristic: the weights are the trained parameters themselves
props.positive_test: gradient updates land on the weights that are used
props.negative_test: another network outputs these weights
props.notes: DEFAULT.

props.characteristic: another network emits these weights
props.positive_test: a generator network's OUTPUT is the target network's parameters
props.negative_test: the weights are trained directly, or copied from a checkpoint
props.notes: Added 2026-10-06. Found twice: a placement agent reported GHN-3 resolving as a plain GNN, losing the point of it, and DynGFN's architectural contribution is a hypernetwork sampler that the diffusion/GFlowNet routing was discarding. Cross-cutting, which is the attribute test: any architecture can have its weights generated.

props.characteristic: which statistic is removed from the activations or weights, and over what it is pooled
props.positive_test: the network contains a layer or weight transform that recentres or rescales using a statistic computed over a declared axis
props.negative_test: a training-time procedure that changes the objective or the data rather than the computation (that is an algorithm); dropping units at random, which is stochastic-regularisation
props.notes: added 2026-10-07 for #95, after the algorithms pinning pass found dropout and batch norm had no home in either dimension. The owner's specification test decides: a thing is a model component if specifying the NETWORK requires it, and an algorithm if specifying the RUN requires it. A normalisation layer is a module with a placement; weight decay is an optimiser argument. Spectral normalisation belongs here too, since W/sigma(W) is what runs at inference

props.positive_test: statistics are pooled over the batch at training time and replaced by running estimates at inference
statistics are pooled over the feature dimension of each example independently, so training and inference behave identically
props.examples: LayerNorm, pre-LN and post-LN transformer blocks

props.positive_test: rescales by a root-mean-square over features with no recentring
statistics are pooled over channel groups within one example, instance normalisation being the one-channel-per-group case
the weight tensor itself is reparameterised by its norm, leaving activations untouched

props.characteristic: what is randomly dropped or perturbed inside the network during training
props.positive_test: the network definition randomly removes or perturbs part of its own computation during training, and the rate is a stated architectural hyperparameter
props.negative_test: adding a term to the objective -- R-Drop and VAT are algorithms although both are built out of dropout; perturbing the data rather than the network
props.notes: added 2026-10-07 for #95. Separate from normalisation because one characteristic per sibling set: normalisation answers what statistic is removed, this answers what is randomly dropped, and they co-occur freely -- a ResNet has batch norm and no dropout, a transformer has layer norm and dropout. Receives the 7 nodes of L.reg.act from the algorithms dimension

props.positive_test: individual activations are zeroed independently at a stated rate
individual weights rather than activations are zeroed
a contiguous or structural unit is dropped as a whole -- a channel, a spatial block, a residual branch, a layer
